quotes.text: Open Stripe Checkout with Managed Payments in a browser to sell in-app digital products or subscriptions.
To process a payment with Managed Payments, all of the products the customer is purchasing must be eligible.
Make sure to store an association on your server between the user account and the Stripe customer ID.
When a customer purchases a subscription through Managed Payments, it only authorizes their payment method to be charged by Managed Payments.

In your [Checkout and Payment Links settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/checkout), configure whether [yearly subscription prices display in monthly terms](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/yearly-price-display.md) and control whether taxes are displayed.

old_evidence.text: You must accept the [Managed Payments terms of service](https://stripe.com/legal/managed-payments) in the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/managed-payments) before you can use Managed Payments.
When a customer purchases a subscription through Managed Payments, it only authorizes their payment method to be charged by Managed Payments.

findings: Both captures describe Stripe-hosted browser Checkout for eligible iOS digital goods or subscriptions in some countries, with Stripe as merchant of record and the Link customer-facing experience. The Merchant of Record role and the app's own user, Stripe Customer and entitlement ledger are distinct. The merchant maps user to Customer server-side to recover purchases, then creates a Checkout Session using a Price in line_items, customer, mode, managed_payments.enabled, origin_context mobile_app and a Universal Link success_url. Compare raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:4-12,125-154,210-256,268-303,514-520 with raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:5-9,142-173,229-276,288-323,536-542. Stripe/Link roles are corroborated by raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-how-it-works-2026-11-07.md:9-29.

All products in the purchase must be eligible, including eligible tax codes, with Dashboard activation, development setup and API 2025-03-31.basil or later in both captures (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:25-43, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:36-54). Some-country external-link scope, product eligibility, StoreKit device purchase restrictions and actual merchant eligibility are separate. The Swift sample checks canMakePayments() for parental controls and opens Safari, and the Universal Link is an app return with a fallback page. User authentication and native StoreKit IAP implementation are outside guide scope. See raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:36-50,175-227,335-379, and wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:13,30-45,51-54. The baseline's 'MoR-compliant' language at line 13 would overstate App Store or regulatory approval.

The baseline summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:38-45 presents checkout.session.completed as sufficient to grant entitlement. Both captures describe server fulfillment after successful payment, map session.customer to the app user and use session.id in a coin transaction example. Redirect can happen after event acknowledgement or after 10 seconds when it is not acknowledged after a successful payment and is an app UI/refresh signal. See raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:341-352,408-467, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:360-373,429-489. The related general Managed Payments guide differentiates completion, asynchronous success and asynchronous failure (raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-2026-11-07.md:398-408, raw/stripe-managed-payments-setup-2025.md:452-464). Conditional on a delayed method being offered, ordinary Checkout's delayed-method guide explains that Session completion can mean debit authorization and to wait for payment success before fulfillment (raw/stripe-checkout-dashboard-payment-methods-2025.md:66-84). Use verified server events and confirm paid outcome before granting credits, with an idempotent per-Session entitlement operation as supported by the reciprocal non-MoR route (wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout.md:25-32). The mobile sample does not prove delayed-method availability, payment or fulfillment execution, or end-to-end idempotency.

The mobile webhook sample is illustrative. It shows signature verification with the raw body using the configured secret, also includes an unsigned fallback, and then references event outside its local declaration instead of the extracted data (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:423-460, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:445-482). This is a retained sample defect/limitation, not a new integration behavior or a production-ready handler. Webhook acknowledgement and entitlement persistence are distinct from the browser return.

Both captures state Managed Payments subscription authorization is limited to charges by Managed Payments and that appropriate consent is needed for transactions outside it (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:493-495, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:515-517). The summary omits this operational boundary (wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:11-45). Preserve the separate app user/Customer mapping and entitlement ownership, and avoid inferring authorization portability or product-level support delegation from the Link checkout identity.

The new section on optional display settings at raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:601-603, tracking/collections/stripe/recollection-2026-11-07-en/pages/7d56148f3e85f3a6f9fe02d8/content.diff:516-526 adds a merchant control for whether yearly subscription prices are displayed in monthly terms and whether taxes are displayed. It describes presentation of prices/tax in Checkout and Payment Links settings, with no stated change to recurring interval, charge amount, or tax behavior. Keep it separate from the session fields and the general Managed Payments tax behavior described in wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-setup.md:50-54.

April uniquely has an explicit Dashboard acceptance requirement for Managed Payments terms of service (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:8-10). The November mobile guide retains activation in its checklist but omits the separate callout (raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:5-9,45-50; tracking/collections/stripe/recollection-2026-11-07-en/pages/7d56148f3e85f3a6f9fe02d8/content.diff:3-11). The April general setup route repeats the terms prerequisite (raw/stripe-managed-payments-setup-2025.md:4-19, wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-setup.md:15-19). The corresponding November general setup intro/checklist also omits that callout (raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-2026-11-07.md:5-16). Retain the April requirement with dates and link scope reciprocally, since omission establishes a documentation change and leaves current legal or account onboarding requirements unresolved.

This is a substantive addition to documented configuration of UI presentation. It leaves the subscription billing interval, amounts and tax treatment unspecified.

Preserve explicit Dashboard acceptance of the Managed Payments terms as dated April guidance (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:8-10), the old raw link and provenance.

Retain the iOS app-to-web, all-product eligibility with eligible tax codes, activation, API-version, one-time/subscription and Customer mapping scope (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:12,25-43,125-154,210-303). Existing app authentication, device permission, browser UI, provider event and merchant entitlement persistence remain distinct.

Retain tested-scenario scope only for card examples, Link passcode and receipt/app visibility (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:469-532, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:491-554). Compare the captured mobile example (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:408-467, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:429-489) to the delayed outcomes in the general Managed Payments Checkout guide (raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-2026-11-07.md:398-408) and the paid-status/verified-webhook qualification in the non-MoR mobile route (wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout.md:25-32). wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:38 describes the same flow as the non-MoR route, and both share Safari and Universal Link shape. However, the Managed Payments guide's examples use the app user's mapped Customer ID in customer, whereas wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout.md:21-28 also documents a separately scoped Accounts v2 customer_account branch and US storefront check. This mobile guide does not resolve actual enabled delayed methods, the order and timing of live payment outcomes, or implementation handling beyond its sample. Cross-reference the captured general route conditionally.

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/set-up-mobile documents one-time or subscription purchases of eligible digital products for iOS users in countries where external payments are permitted. All products in the purchase must qualify, the tax code must be eligible, Managed Payments must be activated in the Dashboard, and the API version must be 2025-03-31.basil or later (new raw lines 5-9 and 36-54). The merchant keeps the server-side app-user-to-Stripe-Customer association and creates a hosted Checkout Session for that Customer with a Price, payment or subscription mode, managed_payments.enabled, origin_context mobile_app and a Universal Link success_url (new raw lines 142-173 and 229-323). The app checks device purchase permission and opens Safari. Stripe provides the merchant-of-record service through the customer-facing Link checkout, and a successful paid flow drives server-side entitlement updates. The return link only brings the customer back to the app, with fallback routing and a possible redirect after an unacknowledged webhook (new raw lines 175-227, 335-379, 429-489 and 536-542). The April capture documents the same flow and explicitly required terms acceptance before use (old raw lines 8-43, 125-154, 210-359 and 408-467). The existing source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md correctly identifies the pair of Session fields and Safari/Universal Link shape, but drops the identity recovery requirement, API and activation prerequisites, paid and verified webhook qualification, and the requirement for separate consent to charge outside Managed Payments after a Managed Payments subscription (new raw lines 515-517, old raw lines 493-495).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/set-up-mobile, the November capture newly documents optional Dashboard controls for monthly presentation of yearly subscription prices and for tax visibility (new raw lines 601-609, old raw lines 534-581). Those settings are presentation controls for prices and taxes, with no stated billing cadence or tax treatment change. The text flow diagram at new raw lines 19-34 elaborates the existing browser, server and webhook flow, while the screenshot locations, Markdown list numbering, JSON layout, sandbox link wording and code formatting are presentation or navigation changes. The April requirement to accept Managed Payments terms in the Dashboard (old raw lines 8-10) disappears from the mobile text while the new prerequisites still say activate Managed Payments (new raw lines 45-50). Keep April terms authority dated and reciprocal with the general Managed Payments setup guide. The omission leaves current terms obligations undetermined. In source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md, keep the API version, some-country scope, app-user-to-Customer identity, separate subscription authorization scope, and paid server outcome boundary. The retained fulfillment example receives checkout.session.completed in its successful-purchase flow (old raw lines 408-467, new raw lines 429-489), while the general Managed Payments setup guide separately documents asynchronous success and failure. Use the reciprocal non-MoR guide for the paid-status and verified server event qualification, without adopting its independently scoped Accounts v2 alternative or claiming that its payment method options apply here. Success URL navigation, device permission and test checkout provide no proof of paid entitlement or current merchant eligibility.
